title: How I Use the Aethelgard Codex
purpose: A practical author reference for turning the Codex into material that actually helps while writing and editing the novel.

workflow.name: Write the scene
workflow.use: Write normally first. The Codex is a reference, not a script.

workflow.name: Check characters
workflow.use: Check family, class, race, personality, relationships, orientation, injuries, equipment, and established history before changing a character.

workflow.name: Check language
workflow.use: Search the language database for an existing word or phrase before inventing a new one. If nothing fits, add a new entry instead of recycling an old word.

workflow.name: Check world terms
workflow.use: Use the glossary, locations, factions, magic, technology, races, and creature atlas to keep terminology consistent.

workflow.name: Continuity pass
workflow.use: Compare the scene against canon rules, timeline, family trees, relationships, geography, injuries, equipment, and previous events.

workflow.name: Editing pass
workflow.use: Only after the scene works should prose, pacing, dialogue, vocabulary, paragraphing, and repetition be polished.

language_rules: Prefer established vocabulary when it exists.
Do not make every invented word share the same syllables or shape.
Keep the fictional language visibly distinct from Common and ordinary English.
Keep romanization stable so translator mappings remain usable.
Record both literal meaning and natural manuscript meaning when they differ.
Use different registers for court, military, ritual, casual, hostile, and intimate speech.
Lyra can understand more than she can comfortably speak because she learned the language from texts rather than conversation.
Do not force language into every sentence; use it where culture, identity, authority, emotion, or communication makes it natural.
relationship_rules: Canon orientation is separate from speculation.
Abel and Elara are established love interests.
Friendship, loyalty, protectiveness, and chosen-family bonds are not automatically romantic.
New romance should add character depth rather than exist only as a label.
editing_warning: The Codex should make writing easier, not trap the author. If a future manuscript passage establishes a new fact, update the database to match it rather than forcing the manuscript to obey an outdated entry.
